proxies.name: rustle
proxies.build: cargo build --locked --release (LTO, no target-cpu, Cargo.lock: as in release.yml)
settings: socket_buffer_bytes = 1048576 (set in the bench config; the shipped default is 0, kernel autotuning)

proxies.name: 3proxy
settings: proxy -a -osTCP_NODELAY -ocTCP_NODELAY (documented for small exchanges; -a = no Forwarded header, like the others)
characteristics: Its best level at 1 KB is 256 connections: it used 19 % of a core at 64 connections and 99 % at 1,024 in the A/B of FAIRNESS.md, hence the concurrency sweep.

Without any socket option it sits in Nagle and a 40 ms delayed ACK (about 1.5k req/s at 1 KB in the A/B): the default config measures a missing documented option, which is why the options above are set.
Supports WebSocket upgrades but spends about 4 ms of CPU per new connection.
Thread-per-connection: uses the n cores of the multi-core curve without a core-count setting.

proxies.name: Squid
proxies.build: from source, upstream's default flags, OpenSSL
settings: http_upgrade_request_protocols WebSocket and websocket allow all (authentication stays enforced by http_access)
characteristics: Authentication is not what limits it at 1 KB: 15,140 req/s with the auth helper against 15,395 without, at 64 connections.
Drops an Upgrade offer unless http_upgrade_request_protocols allows it.
Scales 1 to 8 cores almost as well as rustle (x7.74 against x7.96), from a lower base.

proxies.name: gost
settings: Go sizes GOMAXPROCS from the cpuset
characteristics: Reopens an upstream connection for almost every proxied request (its HTTP handler disables keep-alive by default).
HTTP/2 is a dedicated listener, not ALPN on the TLS port.
Gives the same 2.5k req/s over TLS with or without keep-alive: its overhead is per request, not per connection.

proxies.name: Tinyproxy
characteristics: No upstream keep-alive (documented limitation): it closes the upstream connection after every request.
Removes the Upgrade header (answered 426): no WebSocket support, listed as unsupported, never as zero.
Thread-per-connection with no core-count setting: left out of the multi-core curve.
